what: A quick, picked run of the checks can pass while a unit test that the change breaks is failing. I broke the script that writes the notice on GitHub pull requests (.github/workflows/judge_notice.py) so that it no longer counts removed tests: run by name, two tests in tests/test_judge_notice.py failed, but `python3 checks.py --pick unit` ran no test at all, printed "picked ? of 776 unit tests: the tests that ran the changed Python" and passed. The record that chooses the unit tests (pytest-testmon) sees only code that runs inside the test process, so a Python file that tests start as a separate program (this script, and parts of run.py, checks.py and prove.py that tests run the same way) is treated as reached by no test, though the spec says a change the picker cannot place must run everything, never miss a test.

A picked run of the unit tests can run no test at all and still pass, and it then says "picked ? of 776 unit tests" rather than how many it ran. I ran `python3 checks.py --pick unit` in a copy where nothing had changed since the last whole run: no test ran, the check passed, and its log line records "ran": null. The spec asks that a picked run that would run nothing run a fixed small set and say so, so that a pass never means nothing ran; the browser tests do this with their walks that always run, but the unit check has no such set, and the count it prints is read only from pytest's summary, which says "no tests ran" in this case.
